comparison: Perfect agreement on demographic comparisons (C12, C13). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the findings that antibody titers show no significant differences across sex or age groups. OpenEval notes sample size limitations while peer reviewers implicitly accept without challenge.

Perfect agreement on study group classification (C14-C17). Both evaluations support the selection of 4 sustainers and 4 decliners. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly praises this as a strength, while OpenEval notes the small sample size limits generalizability.

Perfect agreement on the key Tfh finding (C18-C22, C78-C79). Both evaluations strongly support the differential Tfh enrichment between groups. Editor and all peer reviewers describe this as 'solid evidence' using 'multiple methods,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of appropriate molecular characterization.

Perfect agreement on public TCR database analysis (C36-C39). Both evaluations support the findings of comparable frequencies between healthy and COVID-19 cohorts. Peer Reviewer 3 notes this provides 'important fundamental insights,' while OpenEval notes the inference about lack of protective immunity is somewhat speculative but reasonable.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C40-C43, C68, C74). Both evaluations strongly support the correlation between Tfh clonotypes and antibody sustainability. Editor and peer reviewers accept this as the central finding with 'solid evidence,' while OpenEval notes the mechanistic link requires prospective validation.

Agreement on study design and cohort (C2-C4). OpenEval groups these with broader antibody kinetics claims (C5-C11), while peer reviewers separately evaluate cohort characteristics. Both accept the study design without critique.

Strong agreement on antibody kinetics (C5-C11). OpenEval comprehensively evaluates temporal patterns and quantitative decline as well-documented. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge, treating them as valid baseline data for the study's main aims.

Agreement on epitope mapping methodology (C23-C24, C75-C77). OpenEval evaluates the technical rigor and success rates, while peer reviewers focus on the broader achievement. Reviewer 2 calls identifying 78 S epitopes with HLA restrictions 'a major achievement,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of well-established methodology.

Agreement on epitope conservation across variants (C25-C28, C44-C45). Both evaluations support the quantitative conservation analysis and differential responses to mutated peptides. Peer reviewers accept these findings within the broader 'very systemic strategy,' while OpenEval notes functional T cell responses to actual VOC infection would strengthen evidence.

Strong agreement on pre-existing T cell responses (C29-C32, C46-C48, C71-C73). Both evaluations support the diversity findings and differential expansion patterns. Peer Reviewer 3 praises the insights on cross-reactive clones not expanding, while OpenEval emphasizes the clear demonstration of CD8+ expansion versus CD4+ contraction.

Agreement on pre-existing S-reactive T cell characterization (C33-C35). Both evaluations support epitope identification and cross-reactive antigen determination. Peer Reviewer 3 notes this 'nicely showed' cross-reactive clones specific to environmental/symbiotic microbes, while OpenEval notes functional validation of Treg activity would strengthen claims.

Agreement on cross-reactivity source (C53-C54). Both evaluations support the lack of HCoV reactivity and bacterial cross-reactivity findings. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the broader cross-reactivity story, while OpenEval notes the limitation of testing only two clonotypes against HCoV peptides.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretations (C49-C50, C52, C55-C56). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative hypotheses requiring experimental support. Peer reviewers SUPPORT these claims but acknowledge they are presented as speculative, accepting the conclusions about pre-existing clones not expanding.

Agreement on vaccine-induced clonotype dynamics (C57-C59, C69-C70). Both evaluations support the observation that dominant post-vaccination clonotypes were undetectable pre-vaccination. Peer reviewers accept the 'very systemic strategy' and 'solid' conclusions, while OpenEval notes prospective validation is needed for the predictive proposal.

Perfect agreement on literature context (C60-C67 and C1). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited background claims from prior studies. Peer reviewers treat these as standard field knowledge without challenge, and OpenEval notes they support the study's premise but are not novel findings.
